title: Strict direct-image reduction and its completion-unit normalization
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ a finitely generated ideal, $A/I$ additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ finite as a set and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Let $u:U\to V$ be any morphism of schemes. For $T=U,V$ use the small pro-etale site, constant coefficient sheaves, and the unbounded derived category $D(T,A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$, with constant-tower functor $\Delta_T$, and use its ringed diagram-site realization [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Put $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$, $\mathcal R_T(F)=\Delta_TF\otimes^L_{\Delta_T\underline A_T}(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$, and $C_T=\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_T$, with the specified completion unit $\eta$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. Thus an object is complete when its completion unit is invertible. Write $i_{T,F}:\Delta_TF\to\mathcal R_TF$ for tensoring $\Delta_TF$ with the quotient augmentation $\Delta_T\underline A_T\to(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$; under $\mathcal L_T\Delta_TF\cong F$, one has $\mathcal L_T(i_{T,F})=\eta_F$.

Use canonical derived direct image $P=Ru_*$ and total derived termwise direct image $Q=R_u^{\mathcal T}$. Let $\chi_{u,F}:\Delta_V(PF)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\Delta_UF$ be the constant-tower comparison [lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization]. Define $h_{u,F}:\mathcal R_V(PF)\to Q\mathcal R_UF$ by the diagram-site projection morphism adjoint to counit tensored with identity, for $\Delta_UF$ and $(\underline{P_n}_V)_n$, identifying its source through $\chi_{u,F}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Let $b_{u,N}:P\mathcal L_UN\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_VQN$ be the underived-composite normalized direct-image/derived-limit comparison, commuting with all tower projections [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison], and put
$$\rho_{u,F}=b_{u,\mathcal R_UF}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_V(h_{u,F}):C_V(PF)\longrightarrow P(C_UF).$$
For every $F\in D(U,A)$ this is a natural transformation satisfying the equality
$$\rho_{u,F}\circ\eta_{PF}=P(\eta_F).$$
For complete $K$, $h_{u,K}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal T_V)$, natural in $K$, and its $n$-th evaluation is the canonical perfect-$P_n$ projection-formula isomorphism. In particular, as equality of the specified derived morphisms,
$$\mathcal L_V(h_{u,K})\circ\eta_{PK}=b_{u,\mathcal R_UK}\circ P(\eta_K).$$
All equalities are before any evaluation of derived tower morphisms; no uniform cohomological or Tor bounds are imposed.

proof.text:
Put $B_T=(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$. On the diagram sites the projection morphism is natural in both the source object and the coefficient object by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Its value at $\Delta_UF$, followed on the source by the natural constant-tower comparison $\chi_{u,F}\otimes1$, is exactly the specified $h_{u,F}$; consequently $h$ is natural in $F$. Clause (4) of [lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization], with $f=u$ and $M=F$, applies to precisely these constant coefficient sheaves, quotient augmentation and counit-defined diagram projection. It gives, in $D(\mathcal T_V)$,
$$h_{u,F}i_{V,PF}=Q(i_{U,F})\chi_{u,F}.$$
This is an equality of strict derived-tower morphisms, valid for arbitrary $F$.

proof.text:
Write $b_N=b_{u,N}$ and $\chi_F=\chi_{u,F}$. Naturality of the canonical comparison in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison], applied to the actual tower morphism $i_{U,F}:\Delta_UF\to\mathcal R_UF$, gives
$$\mathcal L_VQ(i_{U,F})\,b_{\Delta_UF}=b_{\mathcal R_UF}\,P\mathcal L_U(i_{U,F}).$$
Clause (3) of [lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization] gives $\mathcal L_V(\chi_F)^{-1}b_{\Delta_UF}=1$, under the stipulated constant-tower limit identifications, hence $b_{\Delta_UF}=\mathcal L_V(\chi_F)$. Apply $\mathcal L_V$ to the equality of Step 1, substitute this naturality square, and use the specified $\mathcal L_T(i_{T,H})=\eta_H$. The resulting equality is
$$\mathcal L_V(h_{u,F})\eta_{PF}=b_{\mathcal R_UF}P(\eta_F).$$
Left composition with $b_{\mathcal R_UF}^{-1}$ proves $\rho_{u,F}\eta_{PF}=P(\eta_F)$. Every substitution took place before evaluating any tower morphism.

source.place: Tags 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), 0944 (lemma-projection-formula), and 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), diagram-site proof; agent expansion of fix-lem-exchanges Proof Step 5.

proof.text:
The comparisons $b$ are natural isomorphisms by [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. Together with naturality of $h$ from Step 1 and functoriality of $\mathcal L_V$, this proves naturality of $\rho=b^{-1}\mathcal L_Vh$. Explicitly, for $t:F\to F'$ the naturality squares for $h$ and $b$ give
$$P(C_Ut)\rho_{u,F}=\rho_{u,F'}C_V(Pt).$$
Indeed insert $b_{\mathcal R_UF'}b_{\mathcal R_UF'}^{-1}$ on the left, move $P(C_Ut)$ across $b^{-1}$ using its naturality square, and then move $\mathcal L_V(Q\mathcal R_Ut)$ across $\mathcal L_V(h_{u,F})$ using the square for $h$.

source.place: Tags 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), 0944 (lemma-projection-formula), and 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), diagram-site proof; agent expansion of fix-lem-exchanges Proof Step 5.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$. The perfectness hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum] supplies a bounded finite-projective $A$-complex representing $P_n$. In each degree choose a finite generating surjection from $A^{r}$ and split it by projectivity. The exact constant-module functor and its finite-power identifications [lem-sfb-constant-finite-free-presentation-extension] carry the representing complex and these splitting identities to sheaves. Thus $\underline{P_n}_V$ is represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free $\underline A_V$-modules, so it satisfies precisely the perfectness hypothesis of [lem-sbc-ringed-site-perfect-projection-formula]. That theorem, for $u$, $E=F$ and $P=\underline{P_n}_V$, makes the canonical counit-tensor projection an isomorphism for every $F\in D(U,A)$. In the general augmented-diagram theorem [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate], specialize the coefficient algebra tower to $B_V$ with its unital quotient transitions. Its projection mate, source comparison and augmentation are the ones used here. Its evaluation conclusion identifies $\operatorname{ev}_n(h_{u,F})$ with this very projection morphism, using the canonical constant-coefficient pullback identification. Therefore every evaluation of $h_{u,F}$ is the required perfect-$P_n$ projection-formula isomorphism. The bounded representative was chosen separately for each $n$; no common interval is used.

source.place: Tags 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), 0944 (lemma-projection-formula), and 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), diagram-site proof; agent expansion of fix-lem-exchanges Proof Step 5.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], kernels and cokernels in $\mathcal T_V$ are computed levelwise. Hence for every degree $r$, evaluation identifies $\operatorname{ev}_n H^r(h_{u,F})$ with $H^r(\operatorname{ev}_n h_{u,F})$, which is invertible by Step 4. The kernel and cokernel of $H^r(h_{u,F})$ therefore have every component zero and are zero tower objects. Thus every $H^r(h_{u,F})$ is invertible. The cohomology criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] now implies that $h_{u,F}$ is invertible in $D(\mathcal T_V)$. This proves the required assertion for complete $K$ (and actually for all $F$). Specializing the equality of Step 2 to $F=K$ gives exactly the final displayed equation of the statement. Naturality on complete objects is the restriction of Step 1.

Gave the strict augmentation square, computed its total limit with the normalized constant comparison and naturality of b, proved naturality of rho, and obtained strict invertibility by perfect-coefficient evaluation plus levelwise cohomology. Reused existing general lemmas; no new nodes.

tool_uses.why: The generic ringed-topos derived-limit comparison supplies naturality and the specified underived-composite normalization; it is a tool for the direct-image generator, not a replacement of the compactification route.
Its exact constant-module functor and finite-power identifications turn a bounded finite-projective A-model into a perfect constant coefficient sheaf. This is a site-independent coefficient tool.

The general ringed-site perfect projection formula applies to constant A-sheaves without boundedness or geometric finiteness assumptions. The similarly named adic node uses completed coefficient sheaves and cannot supply this specialization.

The general augmented diagram projection theorem identifies evaluation of the already constructed strict mate with the canonical counit-tensor map; no same-unit statement supplies this evaluation normalization.
Levelwise kernels and cokernels detect invertibility of tower cohomology; this generic abelian-category tool does not change the unit route.
The general cohomology criterion converts invertibility of all tower cohomology maps to invertibility in the unbounded derived category.

The augmented-diagram node's h is the same map (same χ, constant \underline A has f^{-1}R_Y ≅ R_X) and its ev_n is the same counit-tensor projection map.
